transcript: Last night, I saw The Effect at The Shed. This four character play by Lucy Prebble is about a clinical drug trial during which two participants, Tristan and Connie, develop a deep connection. It’s unclear to them, however, if this is just the effect of the drugs and maybe that does or doesn't matter. The other two characters are psychiatrists facilitating the trial and they have their own questions and philosophies about mental health and pharmaceuticals. This production directed by Jamie Lloyd is very minimal and phenomenally acted. The performances really hooked me and sustained my captivation the entire time, despite the somewhat nebulous, almost imaginary setting. But actually, this minimal production design felt appropriately cold and isolating given the themes of the show. I also feel like The Shed is a perfect venue for this show because it gives me similarly clinical and cold vibes. After loving this and Jamie Lloyd's A Doll's House, I'll just say I have high expectations for his Sunset Boulevard coming in next season. With that, another program for my collection.
